The present study examined the relationship between online social connectedness and offline social connectedness in a sample of 183 undergraduate students.

Social networking site users reported significantly higher levels of social connectedness than non-users, and this relationship remained after controlling for the number of friends on their social networking site profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people perceive their social connectedness, and how they derive social connectedness from their use of online social networking sites.
how social connectedness is derived online, and the implications of this for wellbeing.
